item.title: Sigatoka police officer’s death classified as natural after post mortem
item.description: Police say officer’s death was linked to an underlying medical condition, which was exacerbated by personal lifestyle choices. They say foul play has been ruled out based on the findings of the post-mortem examination.
item.content:encoded:
Police say officer’s death was linked to an underlying medical condition, which was exacerbated by personal lifestyle choices.

They say foul play has been ruled out based on the findings of the post-mortem examination.

Police say the findings have been communicated to the officer's next of kin.

Police are calling on members of the public to allow the family to mourn and to avoid spreading speculation about the officer's death.

item.title: Expect the classics and more from The Gang feat. Billy T at Albert Park tonight
item.description: Temalesi Vono , Mikaele Liga · 25/07/2026 Veteran local band The Gang is promising a performance that blends timeless classics with a fresh, modern sound when it takes the stage at Communications Fiji Limited Gratitude Concert at Albert Park this evening.
item.content:encoded:
Temalesi Vono , Mikaele Liga · 25/07/2026

Veteran local band The Gang is promising a performance that blends timeless classics with a fresh, modern sound when it takes the stage at Communications Fiji Limited Gratitude Concert at Albert Park this evening.

Guitarist Conrad Kwan says the band is well prepared and looking forward to performing for concertgoers alongside some of Fiji's biggest musical names.

Remember to bring your family as it is a free concert.

Kwan says fans can expect the songs The Gang is best known for, while also enjoying a contemporary touch that reflects the evolving local music scene.

Drummer Isireli Vulaca describes the concert as a family-friendly event with something for everyone.

He says last year's Gratitude Concert attracted a fantastic turnout, and he hopes this year's event will create even more memorable moments.

Vulaca thanked CFL for continuing to support live music and for providing local artists with the opportunity to perform in front of a large audience.

The Gang, featuring Billy T, will perform at 8.15pm as part of tonight's CFL Gratitude Concert at Albert Park.

Meanwhile, entertainment begins with Dhoom Dhamaka Dance Group performing at 3.05pm, followed by the VITIFM Back2Front Band at 3.30pm.

Sweet Sensation will take the stage at 4.05pm, while the Vude Queen, Laisa Vulakoro, will perform at 5.15pm.

Steve McComber will entertain the crowd at 6.20pm, followed by Seru Serevi at 7pm.

Tauvu Tribute will perform at 7.35pm, followed by The Gang featuring Billy T at 8.15pm.

Savu Ni Delai Lomai will take the stage at 9.20pm, followed by Ju Ben at 9.55pm.

Aggie Vakaloloma will wrap up the night's entertainment at 10.30pm.

item.title: Education Ministry considers deploying final-year students to address teacher shortage
item.description: Minister for Education Aseri Radrodro revealed this to fijivillage News, saying the move is part of the Ministry's efforts to address ongoing staffing shortages. Radrodro says the Ministry is also reviewing teacher placements across schools, districts and divisions to better meet staffing needs.
item.content:encoded:
Minister for Education Aseri Radrodro revealed this to fijivillage News, saying the move is part of the Ministry's efforts to address ongoing staffing shortages.

Radrodro says the Ministry is also reviewing teacher placements across schools, districts and divisions to better meet staffing needs.

He says the shortage is being driven by natural attrition, retirements, resignations and teachers leaving for better opportunities both locally and overseas.

Meanwhile, the Fijian Teachers Association says the number of teacher vacancies has reached 1,000, describing the situation as alarming.

The Association says the growing shortage is largely due to brain drain and stagnant wages, which continue to push qualified teachers out of the profession.

item.title: Fortech wins 2026 Bara Battle champions as Frank Hilton Organisation raises $250,000
item.description: Fortech emerged as the 2026 Bara Battle champions as the Frank Hilton Organisation raised a record $250,000 to support children with disabilities through its residential care services at Albert Park in Suva today. Chief Executive Officer Sureni Perera described the event as an "absolutely amazing" success, saying the organising team was kept busy throughout the day but was encouraged by the overwh
item.content:encoded:
Fortech emerged as the 2026 Bara Battle champions as the Frank Hilton Organisation raised a record $250,000 to support children with disabilities through its residential care services at Albert Park in Suva today.

Chief Executive Officer Sureni Perera described the event as an "absolutely amazing" success, saying the organising team was kept busy throughout the day but was encouraged by the overwhelming support from the crowd and participating corporate teams.

She says every dollar raised will go towards supporting children with disabilities, particularly those living at the Frank Hilton Home.

Perera says the Frank Hilton Organisation provides allied health, education and residential care services to more than 700 children with disabilities every year.

She says the Bara Battle specifically raises funds for the Frank Hilton Home, a 24-hour residential care facility that supports children with very high support needs who do not have families to care for them.

The CEO says the home is staffed by 15 caregivers who provide around-the-clock care, and it costs about $300,000 a year to operate.

She says while the Government provides about 20 percent of the funding, the remaining costs are met through fundraising initiatives such as the Bara Battle.

The CEO says this year's event attracted 25 corporate teams, up from 23 last year, while the amount raised increased from nearly $160,000 in 2025 to a record $250,000 this year.

She highlighted that Team Harcourts and Team Bagel Boys alone raised nearly $120,000, demonstrating the corporate sector's strong commitment to supporting children with disabilities.

Looking ahead, Perera says next year's event will be held in June and will mark the 11th year of the Wheelbarrow Race and the 10th year of the physical race.

She is encouraging more businesses to take part, noting that the $5,000 corporate team entry fee goes directly towards changing the lives of children with disabilities in Fiji.

Meanwhile, Fortech also claimed the Fastest Team title, while TFL won the Speed Walking event in an impressive time of 8 minutes and 29 seconds.

BSP became the first women's team to cross the finish line, while Fiji Payroll (Stands South Pacific Limited), dressed as the iconic Despicable Me Minions, took out the Best Dressed Team award for their creativity and team spirit.

item.title: Families can enjoy a day of music and fun at the CFL Gratitude Concert today
item.description: The Gratitude Concert at Albert Park, organised by Communications Fiji Limited, is expected to attract people of all ages, with families encouraged to come along and enjoy an afternoon and evening of entertainment and fun. The event is being organised as CFL celebrates 41 years of serving its listeners and followers.
item.content:encoded:
The Gratitude Concert at Albert Park, organised by Communications Fiji Limited, is expected to attract people of all ages, with families encouraged to come along and enjoy an afternoon and evening of entertainment and fun.

The event is being organised as CFL celebrates 41 years of serving its listeners and followers.

Entertainment will begin this afternoon at 3pm and continue until 11pm , with food stalls and a bouncy castle adding to the family-friendly atmosphere.

The free event will feature performances by Laisa Vulakoro, Seru Serevi, Steve McComber, Sweet Sensation, Back2Front Band, The Gang featuring Billy T, Savu Ni Delai Lomai, Ju Ben, Aggie Vakaloloma, Tauvu Tribute, and the Dhoom Dhamaka Dance Group .

People can also watch the concert live from 4pm to 11pm on our website, fijivillage and facebook pages, fijivillage and Communications Fiji Limited.

item.title: Charters' court ruling highlights serious flaws and failures in how FICAC acted in charging him and breaching his constitutional rights
item.description: The permanent stay order on the case of Fijian and British national, Charlie Charters by High Court Judge, Justice Pita Bulamainaivalu can be described as a landmark ruling for the country. Charters was charged with two counts of aiding and abetting after allegedly helping a FICAC officer unlawfully publish confidential FICAC information.
item.content:encoded:
The permanent stay order on the case of Fijian and British national, Charlie Charters by High Court Judge, Justice Pita Bulamainaivalu can be described as a landmark ruling for the country.

Charters was charged with two counts of aiding and abetting after allegedly helping a FICAC officer unlawfully publish confidential FICAC information.

Charters was stopped at Nadi International Airport on the morning of Saturday 21st February 2026, driven down by FICAC officers to Suva, taken to the FICAC office in the night, held in custody on Saturday and Sunday, and then charged and presented in court on Monday 23rd February.

The judge ruled today that Charters' right to remain silent was violated by FICAC, Charters' right to freedom of speech, expression, thought, opinion and publication under the 2013 Constitution including not to divulge the sources of his journalistic information was violated by FICAC, there was abuse of process by FICAC, the Commission's case on Counts 1 and 2 of aiding and abetting against Charters will inevitably or doomed to fail, and there is a conflict of interest with regard to count 2.

It was also ruled that Charters' right to remain silent under section 13 of the Constitution must not be qualified by an incentive to divulge his sources of information to negate criminal charges.

Charters had argued that FICAC officers had acted in bad faith and improperly when they initially offered to release him provided he divulges the sources of his journalistic information, and upon Charters refusing to disclose, then coerced and subsequently charged him due to his refusal to divulge his sources of information.

FICAC had argued otherwise in the case that the FICAC officers had acted properly and in good faith when interrogating Charters to reveal the sources of his journalistic information, but did not coerce and subsequently charge Charters for refusing to disclose such information.

Justice Bulamainaivalu said having carefully considered the counsel submissions on point and affidavits, the court finds that Charters has the right to freedom of speech, expression, thought, opinion and publication under section 17 of the Constitution and also not to divulge the sources of his journalistic information, and in the absence of any law to legitimately limit such right pursuant to section 17(3) – (4) of Constitution 2013, that right was therefore violated by FICAC.

Charters had argued that the charges against him are in retaliation to Charters posting and publishing on his facebook account information concerning FICAC, Lavi Rokoika's appointment and conduct as Acting FICAC Commissioner, her husband's access to FICAC premises, and appointment of her niece-in-law as legal officer in FICAC, which retaliatory approach constitutes a violation of his right under section 17(1) of the Constitution 2013 on freedom of speech, expression and publication.

FICAC argued otherwise that Charters' right under section 17(1) of the 2013 Constitution was not violated.

The issue of conflict of interest was also highlighted by Charters where he argued that the particulars of Count 2 mainly concern his report of Rokoika appointing her own niece-in-law, Ulamila Vakalalabure as FICAC legal officer, thus being the subject of the publication and concurrently sanctioning the prosecution of Charters.

Justice Bulamainaivalu said having carefully considered all the evidence, the court concurs with Charters' contention on conflict of interest, which is also indicative of FICAC's failure to properly and thoroughly apply the test for prosecution regarding Charters' criminal matter.

The judge found that the FICAC case against Charters will inevitably or foredoomed to fail because FICAC has failed to identify the person whom Charters allegedly aided and abetted, FICAC breached Charters' right to remain silent and not to self-incriminate, FICAC breached Charters' right to freedom of speech, expression, thought, opinion and publication under section 17 of the Constitution and also not to divulge the sources of his journalistic information.

The judge also highlighted that the particulars of the offence in Counts 1 and 2 are couched in very general and wide terms and not specific enough to allow the defence to discern which evidentiary material in the disclosure correspond to which count.

He said this also prompts the concern of whether Charters, despite pleading not guilty and with legal counsel, did actually understand what the particulars actually meant during the plea stage, and likelihood of succumbing to consequential prejudice to the defence.

Justice Bulamainaivalu said the test for prosecution is whether there is sufficient evidence, and if so, then whether it is in the public interest to prosecute and reasonable prospect of securing a conviction.

He said that the court is of the view that based on its findings, FICAC has not properly and thoroughly applied the test for prosecution, but hastily filed the charges against Charters and at the same time, breached Charters' constitutional rights under sections 13 and 17 of the 2013 Constitution, which are legitimate basis to even exclude other evidence which FICAC lacks.

The judge also said that the defacto officer doctrine bars the court from considering the issues of invalidity of the Acting FICAC Commissioner's appointment and ultra vires acts, which issues are justiciable on a judicial review action pursuant to Order 53 of the High Court Rules 1988.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Charlie Charters says he is delighted that the burden of this FICAC prosecution has been lifted off him.

Charters says this is a major win for journalism and it also recognizes the responsibilities that the State has to protect journalists and citizen journalists.

He says there is also a significant amount of criticism about FICAC, particularly the nature of how they brought the prosecution against him and it failed to meet the critical tests that would normally apply.

Charters says he continues to believe in Fiji and it's potential despite what he has been through in the past few months.
